body:
# Symi Day Trip From Rhodes: Ferry or Organized Tour?

**Short answer:** take the regular ferry if your priority is spending as much independent time as possible in Symi.

Choose an organized boat trip if you also want **St George’s Bay, Panormitis Monastery or hotel transfers** without arranging them yourself.

Do not assume an organized excursion is automatically faster.

Some scheduled ferries between Rhodes and Symi are already very quick.

The real decision is:

**Do you want a day on Symi — or a boat excursion that includes Symi?**

## First, understand what you are booking

A lot of Rhodes booking pages use words such as:

**ferry**

**fast boat**

**day cruise**

**organized tour**

almost interchangeably.

But there are really three different products.

### Regular ferry

You buy transport from Rhodes to Symi and back.

Once you arrive in Gialos, your time is yours.

No group.

No guide.

No compulsory monastery stop.

No scheduled swimming stop.

### Fast-boat excursion

You travel on a tourist boat with a fixed return time.

You normally get a few hours in Symi plus something extra, often **St George’s Bay**.

### Organized Symi + Panormitis tour

The whole day is structured.

You normally get free time in Symi, then continue by boat to **Panormitis Monastery**, sometimes with hotel pickup on Rhodes.

None is automatically better.

They are three different days.

## The independent ferry is better than many people realize

This is the option I would check first.

SEBECO currently operates regular Rhodes–Symi services taking about **1 hour 20 minutes**.

Dodekanisos Seaways also operates the route, with some high-speed 2026 schedules showing Rhodes to Symi in around **50 minutes**.

That means taking a normal ferry does not necessarily condemn you to hours on a slow ship.

It can actually be one of the fastest ways to reach Symi.

And once you arrive, nobody is counting down your three-hour excursion stop.

You decide what to do.

## How much does the ferry cost?

This changes by operator and sailing, so I would always check the current timetable before travelling.

As a useful 2026 reference, SEBECO currently lists standard one-way fares starting around **€17–20**, depending on the service, and also advertises a same-day day-trip fare around **€29–30** on some departures.

The important point is not the exact euro difference.

It is that an independent return ferry can be considerably cheaper than buying an excursion with transfers and additional stops.

If all you want is Symi, paying for a package you do not need makes little sense.

## What do you actually do in Symi?

Most day visitors arrive in **Gialos**, the extraordinary natural harbour lined with pastel neoclassical houses climbing the hillsides.

This is not one of those places where you need a checklist of twelve attractions.

A good few hours can simply mean:

walk the waterfront,

wander into the lanes,

climb part of the way toward Chorio if the heat allows,

have lunch,

look at the boats,

and come back down.

That slow pace is one of the reasons I like the independent-ferry idea.

Symi is a place where having extra free time can be more valuable than adding another attraction.

## Choose the regular ferry if…

I would take the ferry if:

* Symi itself is the reason you are going
* you dislike group schedules
* you want a long lunch
* you want time for photography
* you want to explore beyond the harbour
* you do not care about a scheduled swimming stop
* you have no particular desire to see Panormitis
* keeping the price down matters

For an independent traveller staying in or near Rhodes Town, this is probably the option I would compare first.

## But the ferry does not solve St George’s Bay

This is where organized excursions become interesting.

**Agios Georgios Dysalonas — St George’s Bay — is not another neighbourhood you casually walk to from Gialos.**

It is a dramatic bay below an enormous cliff and is most naturally experienced from the sea.

A popular format from Rhodes combines:

**fast boat to Symi → roughly three hours free in Gialos → swim stop at St George’s Bay → Rhodes.**

That is a very coherent day.

You still get Symi.

But the boat trip itself becomes part of the experience.

## My pick if you want Symi + swimming

One current Viator excursion uses a high-speed boat from Rhodes and takes about **one hour each way**.

You get around **three hours free in Symi**, followed by approximately **30 minutes at St George’s Bay** for swimming.

This is currently one of the most heavily reviewed Symi excursions from Rhodes.



[Fast Boat To Symi with a swimming stop at St George's Bay! (Only 1hr journey)](https://www.viator.com/tours/Rhodes/High-Speed-Boat-To-Symi-Island-Half-Day-Trip/d4272-91578P3?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

I would choose this instead of the regular ferry if St George’s Bay is genuinely part of what I want.

I would not choose it merely because the words “fast boat” sound more exciting.

## Is three hours in Symi enough?

This is probably the most important trade-off.

Three hours is enough to:

walk around Gialos,

have something to eat,

shop,

take photographs,

and explore a little.

It is not a generous amount of time if you want to climb toward Chorio, sit through a leisurely Greek lunch and wander without watching the clock.

Recent traveller discussions about exactly this choice split for that reason.

Some people are perfectly happy with three hours plus St George’s Bay.

Others specifically recommend the regular ferry because they want more control over their time on the island.

Neither group is wrong.

They want different things.

## Panormitis changes the day again

The **Monastery of Archangel Michael Panormitis** is on the opposite side of Symi from Gialos.

So a visit to Panormitis is not a quick walk you add while exploring the harbour.

It requires another boat or land transfer.

That makes organized Symi + Panormitis cruises much more logical.

A typical itinerary gives you several hours in Gialos, then sails around to Panormitis for roughly an hour before returning to Rhodes.

If you genuinely want to see the monastery, that is convenient.

If you do not particularly care about it, it takes time away from Symi.

That is the hidden trade-off.

## My pick if Panormitis matters

Sea Dreams currently runs a Rhodes–Symi–Panormitis day cruise by high-speed catamaran.

The current published schedule is roughly:

**09:00 Rhodes departure**

**10:45 Symi**

**14:00 departure from Symi**

**15:00 Panormitis**

**16:00 departure**

**17:50 Rhodes**

That gives you around three hours in Symi plus the monastery stop.



[Symi island & Panormitis Monastery Self-Guided Tour](https://www.viator.com/tours/Rhodes/Symi-Panormitis-Island-Tour/d4272-29368P21?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

I would choose this if Panormitis is actually on my wish list.

I would not add the monastery simply because the itinerary contains “more”.

## More stops do not automatically make a better day

This is a recurring problem with Greek excursions.

A booking page says:

**Symi + Panormitis + scenic cruise + free time**

and naturally looks better than:

**Rhodes → Symi → Rhodes.**

But every additional stop spends time.

More boarding.

More sailing.

More waiting.

Less freedom.

That is worthwhile when you care about the extra place.

It is not automatically good value just because the itinerary is longer.

## What about St George’s Bay versus Panormitis?

This is actually a very useful decision.

### Choose St George’s Bay if…

You want scenery and swimming.

You like boat days.

You want the cliffs and clear water to be part of the experience.

You do not particularly care about religious or cultural sights.

### Choose Panormitis if…

You specifically want to visit the monastery.

You prefer sightseeing to swimming.

You want to see a second side of Symi.

You are comfortable giving up some Gialos time for it.

### Choose neither if…

What you really want is Symi.

In that case I would take a regular ferry and stop trying to maximize the itinerary.

## If you are staying outside Rhodes Town, the calculation changes

This is where an organized excursion can become worthwhile even if you normally travel independently.

If you are staying in:

Ialysos,

Ixia,

Faliraki,

Lindos,

or southern Rhodes,

getting yourself to the correct harbour early in the morning adds another logistical problem.

Some excursions include or offer hotel transfers.

That can turn a slightly more expensive tour into the easier option.

One current Viator product, for example, includes transfers from selected hotels around Ialysos, Ixia and Rhodes City, then combines around **3.5 hours in Symi** with approximately **one hour at Panormitis**.



[Symi Island from Rhodes with transfers from Ialysos and Ixia](https://www.viator.com/tours/Rhodes/Symi-Island-Cruise-from-Rhodes-with-transfers-from-Ialyssos-and-Ixia/d4272-49323P4?pid=P00320497&mcid=42383&medium=link&medium_version=selector "affiliate-button")

This is the option I would consider when convenience from the hotel matters more than squeezing every possible hour out of Symi.

## Check which Rhodes port you actually need

Do not assume every boat leaves from the same place.

Rhodes has several departure areas used by different services.

SEBECO uses **Kolona Harbour**.

Some tourist excursions use **Mandraki**.

Sea Dreams uses the **Tourist Port** for certain services.

Other high-speed trips can even depart from Faliraki.

This matters more than it sounds when you are standing by the wrong harbour ten minutes before departure.

Check the meeting point on the actual ticket.

Not on a random Google result.

## The fastest option is not necessarily an excursion

This is one booking myth worth killing.

A tourist product may advertise itself as a **high-speed boat**.

That can be perfectly true.

But regular Dodekanisos high-speed ferry schedules have also shown crossings of roughly **50 minutes**.

So choose an excursion for its itinerary.

Not because you assume public transport must be slower.

## What about seasickness?

The Rhodes–Symi crossing is open sea.

Conditions vary.

A bigger conventional ferry and a smaller fast excursion boat can feel different in chop, but I would not promise that one vessel type guarantees a smooth crossing.

Recent traveller reviews include both people describing easy crossings and others reporting significant seasickness.

If you know you are sensitive to motion, look at:

* vessel size
* weather forecast
* where you can sit
* whether you can access fresh air
* total time at sea

rather than trusting a marketing phrase such as “smooth high-speed cruiser”.

## Booking trap #1: confusing “four hours on Symi” with a four-hour trip

When a listing says **four hours in Symi**, that is not the total excursion duration.

You still have:

Rhodes departure,

crossing,

boarding,

return crossing,

and possibly a swim or monastery stop.

Most Symi excursions consume a substantial part of the day.

Treat them as full-day plans.

## Booking trap #2: assuming hotel pickup is included

Sometimes it is.

Sometimes it is an optional surcharge.

Sometimes pickup only covers particular resort zones.

A €50 boat excursion can become something else once transfers from southern Rhodes are added.

Check before comparing prices.

## Booking trap #3: choosing Panormitis because it is included

This is perhaps the strangest one.

Do not visit a monastery simply because a tour happens to stop there.

Look at photographs.

Read what Panormitis is.

Decide whether you actually want to spend an hour there.

If the answer is no, choose a different boat and give that time back to Symi.

## Booking trap #4: ignoring the return schedule

With an independent ferry, the outbound crossing is only half the decision.

Check the **same-day return** before buying anything.

Ferry timetables vary by season and weekday.

A wonderful cheap outbound fare is useless if the only suitable return does not fit your day.

Build the trip around the pair of sailings.

Not one ticket.

## Which would I choose?

### First visit to Symi

If I mainly wanted to see the island:

**regular ferry.**

I would rather have freedom in Gialos than another scheduled stop.

### First visit + I love swimming

**Fast boat + St George’s Bay.**

That is a genuinely different experience and justifies giving up some independent time.

### Culture rather than swimming

**Symi + Panormitis.**

The monastery makes sense as part of a structured excursion.

### Staying in Ixia or Ialysos

I would compare the price of an organized trip with hotel pickup against ferry + taxi/bus logistics.

Convenience may win.

### Staying in Lindos or southern Rhodes

I would pay particular attention to transfer arrangements.

Getting to Rhodes Town and back can turn a “simple ferry trip” into a much longer day.

### I hate being rushed

Regular ferry.

Easy decision.

## Dan's recommendation

I have not taken these particular Symi excursions myself.

I compared current 2026 ferry schedules, operator itineraries and recent traveller experiences because “day trip to Symi” hides several very different products.

My default choice would be surprisingly simple:

**take the ferry if Symi itself is what you want to see.**

You do not need an organized tour merely to reach the island.

The ferry gives you freedom and can be remarkably quick.

I would switch to an excursion for one of three reasons:

**St George’s Bay.**

**Panormitis.**

**Hotel transfer convenience.**

Those are real benefits.

“Organized tour” by itself is not.

So before booking, ask:

**Am I trying to spend a day in Symi — or am I trying to fit several experiences into one day?**

That answer will usually choose the boat for you.

*Some links on this page are affiliate links. If you book through them, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.*

**Checked: 27 October 2026.**

subtitle: You can reach Symi independently by ferry or book a day cruise with St George’s Bay, Panormitis or hotel transfers. Here is which option gives you more time on Symi — and when a tour is actually worth paying for.
title: Symi Day Trip From Rhodes: Ferry or Organized Tour?
